correctness.rationale: For degree d and s agreeing ordinary neighbors, a legal closed-neighborhood minority flip changes E=2 times monochromatic edges by 2(d-2s). All rim degrees are three, hence every rim flip decreases E by at least two; only the hub, when n even, can flip neutrally. A neutral-energy plateau has at most two states; with a,b active rim counts the first-step equations (a+1)e0=N+e1 and (b+1)e1=N+e0 imply maximum expected exit time 3N, N=n+1. At most E(c)/2 strict drops yields the claimed expected-time bound. For hub bit fixed, rim inactivity excludes cyclic 00 and 111, giving n/z*binom(z,n-2z) by distinguished-zero/gap counting and Perrin total by 3-state transfer. Alternating rims yield precisely the two nonabsorbing 2-cycles. Independently built all-state Markov transitions and sink SCCs for n=3..8; total recurrent states, component sizes, and every z-profile matched, without using finite checks to imply all n.
residual_risks: Checks are bounded; infinite claims rest on reconstructed proof.

final_claim: For every n>=3, uniform asynchronous closed-neighborhood minority on the wheel W_n has exactly 2P_n recurrent configurations with refined rim profile B(n,z)=n/z*C(z,n-2z): odd n has only absorbing states, even n has two hub-flipping pairs and 2P_n-4 singletons. Every start has expected time to a recurrent class <=(3/2)(n+1)E(c)<=6n(n+1).
